question.problem:
Compute the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by the vectors $x=⟨2,3,0⟩$, $y=⟨1,4,5⟩$, and $z=⟨0,2,6⟩.$

$V=${{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The volume of a parallelepiped spanned by three vectors is given by the absolute value of their triple product.

First, we compute the triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}|-3\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(4\cdot 6-5\cdot 2)-3(1\cdot 6-5\cdot 0)+0 \\  & =2(24-10)-3(6) \\  & =28-18 \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the absolute value. So, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped is 

$$
V=|10|=10.
$$
